transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jenna (Crestline Head of ML Ops), Marcus (Crestline VP Eng), Priya (Crestline Platform)

Summary: Quarterly business review, focus on current usage trends, unexpected costs in April, reliability incidents (2 outages in past quarter), roadmap ask for dedicated capacity and VPC/private deployment options, compliance questions (audit logs, KMS). Next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- Usage and cost trends (April spike)
- Reliability incidents and mitigations
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (latency, cost, SLA)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, audit logs, KMS, SSO)
- Roadmap and pilot/POC for Dedicated capacity

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes today, qbr focused on usage, costs and reliability — quick roll call?
00:08 Jenna: hi jenna here, yea we've got a few people on, marcus and priya are on as well
00:12 Marcus: hey all, glad to be here
00:14 Priya: hi, thanks
00:16 Maya: great, i'll kick off with a 5 minute recap of what we've seen then ravi will go into perf and liam will cover support/ops briefly
00:30 Maya: so quick context: crestline's been on Redwood hosted standard tier since jan, you ramped production for recommendations in march, and april had that unexpected cost bump that we want to unpack
01:02 Priya: yeah the april bill was higher than forecast, especially token costs for the rerank route, we saw a couple of traffic bursts when a campaign hit and it really spiked token usage
01:18 Liam: right and support saw two incidents, one was a degraded latency window after an ops deployment and the other was a brief fallback to the smaller model when capacity throttled, logging shows automatic fallback fired at 04:12 UTC on 4/12
01:34 Ravi: i pulled the runtime traces, the higher tail latency correlated with longer context lengths from that campaign; batching wasn't as effective because requests were more bursty and short-lived, so per-token cost went up due to re-creating KV caches often
02:05 Marcus: how much of that would be solved by dedicated capacity? like is this a capacity problem or a prompt/engineering problem?
02:18 Ravi: it's a mix — dedicated capacity gives you predictable throughput and eliminates noisy neighbor issues; also you can tune batching and pre-warm KV caches for your common prompt shapes. But prompt engineering to reduce unnecessary context would also help cost a lot
02:42 Jenna: our ops team is hesitant to switch to dedicated without clear ROI — can you show the delta in costs for our current monthly spend vs 3 node dedicated pool?
02:55 Maya: absolutely we'll send a modelled comparison. initial estimate based on current usage looks like dedicated could reduce unit cost by 20-35% depending on utilization and quantization profiles
03:22 Priya: question on private deployment: we have regulatory concerns around PCI-ish data and want VPC peering / customer-managed KMS; is that available?
03:35 Liam: yes we support VPC/private deployment options; for the private offering we give customer-managed KMS integration and audit logs. i'll attach the security pack after the call but quick answer is yes, it's supported
03:50 Marcus: and how about SSO and RBAC for multiple teams? we have 30 engineers who need role separation
03:57 Maya: SAML SSO and granular RBAC is included in enterprise tiers, you can map roles to teams and route quotas per-team
04:12 Jenna: there was one reliability event where the model fell back to the 7B variant — that impacted customer experience, can you explain fallback policy?
04:28 Ravi: sure — by default requests can fallback to compatible model variants if the primary model isn't available; the policy is configurable per-route with strictness levels. in your case, fallback was enabled and defaulted to keep serving. we can tighten it so it returns 503 instead if you prefer strict consistency
04:52 Priya: we prefer consistent model output, 503 is preferable to silent variant fallback for some routes
05:00 Maya: noted — we'll propose route-level fallback policies in the recommendations
05:10 Marcus: what's the SLA on dedicated vs hosted? we care about p99 latency and availability guarantees
05:18 Liam: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and tighter latency targets, hosted has good SLOs but not the same contract. we can include p99 latency targets in a dedicated contract based on the pool size
05:33 Jenna: i want to dig into the april token spike — can you show us which prompts/routes drove it?
05:40 Ravi: yes the rerank and summarization routes accounted for about 72% of token consumption that month; the rerank route in particular had longer lists and reprocessed older requests during the campaign which created a lot of repeated context
06:05 Priya: we can share the sample traffic and the prompt templates after the call, we'll scrub PII
06:10 Maya: perfect, that will help us create batching and cache rules plus pre-warm strategies
06:20 06:35 Maya: short demo of what we'll recommend (Maya describes on call) — for rerank we suggest incremental reranking and caching top-k results, avoid full-document re-embedding when possible, and for summarization use smaller context windows + selective retrieval
07:12 Marcus: if we reduce context, does that impact quality? we can't lose critical info for compliance summaries
07:22 Ravi: tradeoff, yes; we can do targeted retrieval to surface only regulatory-relevant sections and keep a much smaller working context. also evaluation harness can help: we can run quality regressions to ensure thresholds are met before rollout
07:45 Jenna: can Redwood run those evals on our behalf? we need a before/after comparison for the team
07:50 Maya: we can run evals as part of the Optimize package — we'll include a proposal for sample tests and acceptance criteria
08:03 Marcus: competitors question — we've been kicked on anthro/vertex pricing, how do you stack vs them on tail latency and cost?
08:12 Ravi: compared to managed vertex endpoints, Redwood's strength is the unified runtime optimizations and smart routing; for tail-latency we can tune kernels and batching aggressively on dedicated, plus prefix/KV cache yields big gains for repeated context patterns. Anthropic has different model tradeoffs but we can run side-by-side benchmarks if you want
08:35 Priya: yes that would help our infra team in the eval matrix
08:40 Maya: we'll include a benchmark plan in the follow up
08:44 09:00 Jenna: about audit logs and retention, we need 12 months retention for request logs and the ability to export them to our SIEM
09:10 Liam: audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to SIEM via our integration; retention windows are configurable for enterprise accounts, we'll include the exact mechanics in the security pack
09:25 Priya: on encryption, do you support customer-managed HSM for encryption-at-rest keys?
09:31 Liam: yes we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management in private deployments; hosted can also be configured with CMKs where required
09:40 Marcus: okay on costs, if we sign up dedicated what's the typical commit term? monthly or annual? and is there a ramp allowance?
09:50 Maya: we offer monthly reserved pools and discounted annual commits — ramp allowance and burst credits can be included in the contract during the first 90 days to help with unpredictable campaigns
10:05 Jenna: we have a procurement timeline — if we decide to move forward, we need pricing and contract review by end of june
10:12 Maya: that aligns with our sales timeline, we'll target that. action items noted
10:20 Priya: one technical doc ask — what telemetry do we need to provide to get the best batching? is there a format for the traffic sample?
10:29 Ravi: csv with timestamps, route name, context length, and payload size is ideal; we'll share a template. key fields: user id hashed, request id, context tokens, response tokens, and timestamp
10:45 Jenna: can you also show us where to set per-route fallback and per-route quantization profiles in the console? we want to self-serve some ops changes
10:55 Maya: yes console has route-level controls for fallback strictness, quantization presets and autoscale policies; we'll record a quick walkthrough or schedule a short demo if you'd prefer
11:12 Marcus: on the roadmap, which features are coming that would reduce our cost or improve reliability?
11:20 Ravi: near-term: better prefix caching heuristics, smarter KV reuse across short-lived sessions, plus more quantization profiles for 16k+ context models; medium term: model variant routing (auto choose cheaper equivalent for non-sensitive routes) and larger private deployment tooling for on-prem
11:44 Priya: timeline for prefix caching improvements?
11:48 Ravi: Q3 roadmap for rollout to hosted, earlier for dedicated customers in pilot starting late q2
11:54 Jenna: ok that's helpful
12:00 Maya: ok quick recap of next steps — maya will send cost model and deck, liam send security pack, ravi run benchmark, priya to share traffic, we schedule dedicated pricing call next week
12:15 Marcus: thanks all, that sounds good
12:18 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and an invite.
